figure_caption: Overview of the width-dependence test. Delay is the gap between the first checkpoint at which training accuracy reaches 0.99 and the first at which held-out accuracy does, floored at one probe interval (250 steps) and set to the step limit (10,000) if either threshold is never reached (censored). The slope of ln(delay) against log2(width) is estimated over five widths and four seeds, with a seed-cluster bootstrap interval; the interval, not the point estimate, determines the verdict. In this study the slope is -0.020 with interval [-0.585, 0.354], which straddles zero, so the verdict is inconclusive.

panels.title: Delay and censoring
panels.short_caption: Each run's delay is the gap between fitting the training pairs and generalizing, floored at 250 steps and capped (censored) at 10,000.
panels.drawio_prompt:
SINGLE IDEA: one training run (width d, seed s) is reduced to a single delay number, with a floor and a censoring cap.

NODES (stable IDs):
- run: rounded box 'Run (d, seed)' — process; input of the panel (top-left).
- curves: a deferred matplotlib inset [[mp:acc_curves]] — a qualitative accuracy-vs-step plot with two rising curves: a training-accuracy curve that rises early and a held-out-accuracy curve that rises much later; a horizontal dashed threshold line at 0.99; two vertical drop-lines/markers at the first crossings labelled $$t_{fit}$$ (train) and $$t_{gen}$$ (held-out), and a horizontal double-headed bracket between them labelled $$\Delta$$. X-axis 'step (probe every 250)', y-axis 'accuracy'. Message is only: train crosses first, held-out crosses later, gap = delay. No numeric ticks except 0.99.
- both: diamond decision 'Both reach 0.99?' — decision node.
- d_ok: sharp box (data/result) 'max(t_gen − t_fit, 250)' — floor applied; small tag 'floor = 1 probe'.
- d_cens: sharp box (result), visually flagged as the censored/special outcome: '10,000' with tag 'censored (cap)'.
- ln: small rounded box '$$\ln\Delta$$' — the value passed on to the regression panel (right edge, with an outgoing stub arrow to the panel border labelled 'to regression').
- note: one short text 'Censored runs kept, never dropped'.

EDGES:
- run → curves (solid, 'checkpoints every 250 steps, 40 total' — keep as short label '40 checkpoints').
- curves → both (solid).
- both → d_ok (solid, label 'yes').
- both → d_cens (solid, label 'no (either never)').
- d_ok → ln (solid); d_cens → ln (solid).

LAYOUT: left-to-right reading. Run at top-left, curves inset large beneath/right of it as the visual anchor (about half the panel), decision diamond to its right, the two outcome boxes stacked (d_ok above, d_cens below) right of the diamond, merging into ln at the right edge. note sits under d_cens.

IMPORTANCE: curves inset and the two outcome boxes (floor vs cap) are most important; run and note least.

TEXT BUDGET (exact labels only): 'Run (d, seed)', '40 checkpoints', 'accuracy', 'step', '0.99', '$$t_{fit}$$', '$$t_{gen}$$', '$$\Delta$$', 'Both reach 0.99?', 'yes', 'no (either never)', 'max(t_gen − t_fit, 250)', 'floor = 1 probe', '10,000', 'censored (cap)', '$$\ln\Delta$$', 'to regression', 'Censored runs kept, never dropped'.

panels.title: Slope and seed-cluster bootstrap
panels.short_caption: ln(delay) is regressed on log2(width) over 5 widths x 4 seeds; seeds are resampled as clusters to get a 95% interval. This run: slope −0.020.
panels.drawio_prompt:
SINGLE IDEA: ln(delay) is regressed on log2(width) across 20 runs, and the slope's uncertainty comes from resampling whole seeds.

NODES (stable IDs):
- scatter: a deferred matplotlib plot [[mp:slope_schematic]] — SCHEMATIC (explicitly not data): x-axis 'log2(width)' with five ticks labelled 16, 32, 64, 128, 256; y-axis '$$\ln\Delta$$'. Two horizontal reference lines: lower 'floor ln 250' and upper 'cap ln 10,000'. At each of the five x ticks a small vertical group of 4 generic points (one per seed, four distinct marker shapes or tints for seeds), with a few points sitting exactly on the cap line drawn as hollow/flagged 'censored'. One straight OLS line through the points, labelled $$\beta$$. Qualitative message only: points confined between floor and cap, one fitted line, censored points sit at the cap. No numeric y ticks.
- ols: rounded box 'OLS slope $$\beta$$' — process, below/next to scatter.
- boot: rounded box 'Seed-cluster bootstrap' with tag '2,000 resamples' — process. Beneath it a small glyph of four seed columns (201–204) being redrawn with replacement, each column keeping all five widths (draw as 4 small stacked-bars labelled 'seed' with a curved arrow 'resample with replacement').
- ci: sharp box (result) '95% interval' with tag '2.5–97.5 percentile'.
- thisrun: highlighted result marker (this run's outcome, emphasised): '$$\beta = -0.020$$' and '[−0.585, 0.354]', with tag '8 of 20 runs censored'.

EDGES:
- (panel-left stub) → scatter (solid, label '$$\ln\Delta$$ per run').
- scatter → ols (solid).
- ols → boot (solid).
- boot → ci (solid, label '2,000 slopes').
- ci → thisrun (solid) ; ols → thisrun (dashed, labelled 'point').
- ci → (panel-right stub) (solid, label 'to verdict').

LAYOUT: scatter on top, ~50% of panel height, wide. Below it a left-to-right strip: ols → boot → ci. thisrun sits at bottom-right under ci, outlined as the run outcome.

IMPORTANCE: scatter and thisrun are the focal elements; boot is second; ols and ci third.

TEXT BUDGET (exact labels only): 'log2(width)', '16', '32', '64', '128', '256', '$$\ln\Delta$$', 'floor', 'cap', 'censored', '$$\beta$$', 'OLS slope $$\beta$$', 'Seed-cluster bootstrap', '2,000 resamples', 'resample seeds with replacement', '95% interval', '2.5–97.5 percentile', '$$\beta = -0.020$$', '[−0.585, 0.354]', '8 of 20 runs censored', 'to verdict', 'schematic'.

panels.title: Pre-declared verdict rule
panels.short_caption: The interval, not the point estimate, maps to supported / inconclusive / refuted; this run's interval straddles zero, so the verdict is inconclusive.
panels.drawio_prompt:
SINGLE IDEA: the verdict depends only on where the 95% interval of the slope sits relative to zero; this run's interval straddles zero.

NODES (stable IDs):
- axis: a horizontal slope axis labelled '$$\beta$$ (slope)' with a vertical dashed zero line labelled '0', spanning the full panel width. Negative side left labelled 'delay shrinks with width', positive side right labelled 'delay grows with width'.
- rule_sup: row 1 — a generic interval glyph (horizontal bar with end caps) lying entirely left of zero, followed by a verdict tag 'Supported' and a short condition 'interval < 0'.
- rule_inc: row 2 — a generic interval glyph straddling the zero line, tag 'Inconclusive', condition 'straddles 0'.
- rule_ref: row 3 — a generic interval glyph entirely at/right of zero, tag 'Refuted', condition 'interval ≥ 0'.
- thisrun: row 4 (or overlay on row 2) — this run's measured interval as an emphasised glyph: bar spanning from '−0.585' to '0.354' across the zero line with a dot at '−0.020'; labelled 'This study'. A bold marker/arrow ('◀ this study') ties it to rule_inc.
- verdict: a prominent result badge 'Verdict: inconclusive' attached to rule_inc and thisrun (the outcome of this run).
- note: small text 'Decided by the interval, not the point estimate' under the axis.

EDGES:
- (panel-left stub 'from bootstrap') → thisrun (solid).
- thisrun → rule_inc (solid, label 'matches').
- rule_inc → verdict (solid).
- rule_sup and rule_ref: no outgoing edges; they are shown as the unmatched alternatives (drawn de-emphasised).

LAYOUT: three rule rows stacked top-to-bottom on a shared slope axis so the zero line is one continuous vertical dashed line through all rows; Supported on top, Inconclusive in the middle, Refuted at bottom (rows ordered by interval position left → right). thisrun glyph drawn on the same axis directly aligned with the middle row and highlighted; verdict badge at the right of the middle row. Rows' interval glyphs are generic illustrations, labelled no numbers except on thisrun.

IMPORTANCE: the middle row, thisrun glyph and the verdict badge are the focal elements (this run's outcome); the other two rows are secondary context.
